About 560 real sound-chip instructions used to kill the emulator; they are now properly implemented and graded against 1,268,000 known-good cases. Two fresh reviewers on a private off-screen display: one tries jobs a newcomer would want done with only the README to go on and logs every place it gets lost, one walks every panel and message against a checklist. Runs after the fixes in flight land; nothing appears on your screen.

FIXED AND GREEN. Your automated checks ran and passed for the first time since 22 July. Three separate breakages had to go, the third only visible once the first two were cleared. The run's log now names each of the six data checks as it passes, so a future green cannot be a green of nothing.

queue.title: FIXED and landed. A reset could strand your save, or write an older one over a newer one. Now proved by two tests that read the actual file on disk -- the old test for this checked the emulator's memory and never the file, which is why it passed for so long. Still worth one live check when your window is up: I proved the mechanism, not the keypress.

Two video writes in one instruction charge the first one's delay twice -- 40 percent over-billed on the most common way games write video memory. The read path next door does it correctly. Every existing test stops one write short of triggering it.

The rest of the lens sweep: 8 critical, 33 high, ~77 smaller, all in docs/superpowers/notes/2026-09-06-oracle-lens-sweep.md with the derivation for each. Nothing is fixed -- the reviewers were read-only on purpose so the report stays honest. Most of these have their fix already written elsewhere in the tree; they are gaps in coverage, not in knowledge.

queue.title: Your lag report. The plane viewer only redraws when its picture changes -- but on the waterline and floor-fan rows the picture changes every frame by design, so it redraws the whole plane every frame and the saving never applies. Up to half a million pixel lookups per frame. Not confirmed as YOUR lag yet; the tab test confirms or clears it.

Waiting on you, and it is the one that holds the rest up: both ways of showing a headline number are on the Pacing tab of the build now on your screen. Say A or B and the other is deleted. Full text in docs/2026-09-06-queue-detail.md.
The remaining panels follow your A/B answer plus four things only your eyes can settle. I am running them past you one at a time rather than in a batch.
Say 'install the icon' and I write five icon files and one desktop entry under your home. Nothing else is touched and the dry run is exact.
Your call on refreshing our frozen copies of the game's symbol files. I recommend holding until the engine team publishes a build manifest; the silent-drift fault itself is already fixed and landed.
Toy Story is silent here and I have ruled out the obvious causes, so the gap is inside our sound emulation. The next question is cheap and yours: does the OLD emulator play it with sound?

The next thing I would build, and it is owed rather than chosen: when something swaps the machine out from under a connected tool, the tool is currently never told, so it keeps reading a world that no longer exists. The contract team already adopted our request for this.

The reason I keep having to ask you to look at panels instead of reading them myself: the window can report its top bar to a connected program but not any panel. Fixing it converts a class of 'please look at this' into something I can measure.
